Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Intake Brief: Challenges as achievements — sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements

## Problem statement

The engine's challenge system (per-run meta-goals, e.g. Main Street's "Foodie Row") is conceptually a form of achievement. Once the Steam version exists (Electron launcher with Steamworks), challenge completions should sync to Steam achievements so players earn persistent, account-level recognition visible on their Steam profile and in the overlay.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn Steam achievements for completing in-game challenges; see progress on their Steam profile.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — an engine-generic achievement layer so any game can map its challenges to Steam achievements without writing Steam SDK code.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want the challenges I complete in Main Street (and future games) to appear as Steam achievements, so my progress is recognised beyond the run itself.
- As a TCE developer, I want a game-agnostic achievement layer in the engine, so adding achievements to a new game is declarative (challenge → achievement mapping) with no Steam SDK code in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An **engine-generic achievement layer** exists in the core engine (extending the existing generic `ChallengeSystem` model): games define achievement definitions (id, title, description, hidden flag) and map challenge completions to achievements. This layer is pure engine code with no Steam dependency (works headless / in the web build).
2. When a challenge is completed inside the Steam launcher, the mapped Steam achievement is unlocked via Steamworks (`ISteamUserStats::SetAchievement` + `StoreStats`); verified by automated tests with a mocked Steamworks session and a documented manual E2E check with a real Steam account.
3. Steam sync is **idempotent and offline-safe**: unlocked achievements persist locally, are re-synced to Steam when available, and the launcher never crashes when Steam/Steamworks is absent (graceful degradation, consistent with the follow-on-Steam feature CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
4. A single **achievement manifest** (game id ↔ achievement id ↔ Steam API name, hidden flag) is the source of truth and matches the static Steam store configuration; mismatch detection is documented.
5. **Main Street is the first consumer**: all 12 challenge templates (`MainStreetChallenges.ts`) are mapped to Steam achievements through the generic layer (no Steam SDK code in the game module).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Timing:** Steam sync is implemented only when the Steam version exists — blocked by the Electron launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) and the Steamworks integration introduced by the follow-on-Steam incentive (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC). The engine-generic achievement layer itself can be designed/built now; the Steam bridge lands with Steamworks.
- **Engine-generic (user decision):** no game-specific Steam code; games declare achievements via the generic layer; Main Street first.
- **Steam backend reality:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steam store backend with static API names (App ID + achievement list). The manifest must match that configuration; store setup itself lives outside this repo.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies (Steamworks SDK usage follows the pattern set by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` / `ActiveChallengeRecord<TState>` interfaces plus generic selection/evaluation; game-agnostic by design ("M6 extraction" notes already anticipate reuse).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — the only consumer: 12 challenge templates across 5 categories, per-run selection (`selectChallenges`), evaluation with completion callback that pushes to `state.challengesCompleted` and the activity log. Challenges are run-local and non-persistent.
- No achievements, no Steam SDK code, no Electron code in the repo today. Steamworks integration is being introduced by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC into the launcher from CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC explicitly defers this scope: "Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item."

## Desired change

1. Add an **achievement concept to the core engine** (new module, e.g. `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`, or an extension of `ChallengeSystem`): achievement definitions, a completion-event surface, and a persistence-agnostic "unlock" registry that the web build can use without Steam.
2. Define the **achievement manifest** for the launcher (`electron/steam-achievements.ts`): game/achievement ids ↔ Steam API names + hidden flags, documented to match the Steam store backend config.
3. Add the **Steam bridge** in the Electron main process: renderer reports achievement-unlocked events via preload/IPC; main process calls Steamworks `SetAchievement`/`StoreStats`; local persistence of unlocked ids with later re-sync; graceful degradation without Steam.
4. **Wire Main Street** as the first consumer: a declarative mapping from the 12 challenge templates to Steam achievements, fired from the existing challenge-completion path.
5. Tests (mocked Steamworks session; headless unit tests for the engine layer) + documentation (README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` as needed).

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` (new) — generic achievement definitions + unlock registry + completion-event surface (no Steam dependency).
- `src/core-engine/index.ts` — barrel exports for the new module.
- `electron/steam-achievements.ts` (new) — achievement manifest (ids ↔ Steam API names) + Steamworks sync bridge.
- `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.ts` — IPC surface for achievement-unlock events from the renderer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` (or a new `MainStreetAchievements.ts`) — mapping of the 12 challenge templates to achievements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (engine layer, manifest matching) + mocked-Steamworks sync tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — Steam achievements workflow documentation.

## Related work

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Tutorial Coverage for Action Banking (Contextual First-Bank Trigger)

## Problem statement

The action banking mechanic is fully implemented and visible in the HUD (banked-action counter + tooltip), but the 23-step Main Street tutorial never mentions or teaches it. The prior plan embedded banking text statically in T6 (first End Turn). Revised scope: replace the fixed insert with a **contextual, first-time trigger** that fires when the player ends a turn with remaining action points, so the lesson lands when banking actually happens. Staff-first consumption copy must also be softened: note that while some staff grant action points, the player likely won't have any at that early stage.

## Users

- **New players** completing the Main Street tutorial — they need to understand that saving actions across days is a strategic option, not wasted turns, and that the banking lesson should appear at the moment it becomes relevant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Contextual first-bank trigger:** When the tutorial is active and the player ends a turn with `state.actionsRemaining > 0` (i.e., at least one unused action would bank), a banking hint/step fires exactly once — the first time this condition is met. It does not fire when the player spends all actions, and never fires a second time. Must not block the end-of-turn flow (`processEndOfTurn` still runs).
- 2. **Persistence flag:** Tutorial state gains a persisted flag (e.g., `hasSeenBankingHint` / `bankingHintShownAt`) so the hint is not repeated across sessions/restarts. Flag defaults to false for legacy saves and is set on first trigger; cleared only by explicit tutorial reset.
- 3. **Staff-first consumption softened:** Tutorial copy covering staff-derived actions states the general rule (staff actions like General Manager's +1 are spent first and never bank themselves) but adds the early-game caveat that the player likely has no such staff yet, so the current bank is from unused base actions.
- 4. **Banking concept + cap + HUD highlight:** Hint/step copy explains unused actions bank up to a cap of 2 and are carried into future days, and highlights the banked-action count in the HUD action counter (e.g., "(1 banked)" suffix) so players learn where to check their reserve.
- 5. **i18n keys added:** New/updated tutorial text keys registered in `tutorial-en.ts` following the `tutorial.<stepId>.title` / `tutorial.<stepId>.body` pattern (or `tutorial.bankingHint.*` for the contextual hint); no hardcoded card names/costs.
- 6. **No regressions:** Existing 23-step tutorial flow, copy, and gate logic remain unchanged except for the additive contextual hint; all existing tests pass. Editorial rules hold (≤3 sentences per box, one point per box).

## Constraints

- **Tutorial-only changes:** No core-engine, card-system, rule-engine, or UI component changes beyond the narrow persistence field and trigger wiring inside Main Street's tutorial layer. Banking cap (2) and engine accounting unchanged.
- **Editorial rules apply:** ≤3 sentences per text box, exactly one point per box; no time-limited play mentions; no hardcoding of card names/costs in step strings that could go stale.
- **Trigger placement:** Banking lesson is NOT a fixed insert (no static T6 body edit for banking). It is a contextual overlay/step triggered from the turn-controller's end-turn path, gated on `actionsRemaining > 0` and the persistence flag. Staff-first wording update is a copy tweak on the relevant step/hint (not a new step).
- **Action banking is already implemented:** All engine, state, HUD, and tooltip work from CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR and its children is complete.

## Existing state

- **HUD:** `MainStreetRenderer.ts` renders the action counter as `<remaining> action(s) left` with a `(<banked> banked)` suffix when `bankedActions > 0`.
- **Tooltip:** `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` `buildActionTooltip()` explains banking and appends a GM note when employed.
- **Tutorial:** 23 steps (T1–T23), defined in `TutorialFlow.ts` (`UNIFIED_TUTORIAL_STEPS`), copy in `tutorial-en.ts`. Step T6 is the first End Turn. Persistence lives in `TutorialState.ts` (`MainStreetTutorialStateV1`, schema v1, localStorage).
- **Turn flow:** `scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` `endTurn()` gates via `isTutorialActionAllowed`, sets `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` for T6, then calls `processEndOfTurn`.
- **Engine banking:** `MainStreetEngine.ts` `processEndOfTurn` banks `min(actionsRemaining,1)` capped at 2; `executeDayStart` composes `1 + gmBonus + min(banked,2)` into `actionsRemaining`.
- **Editorial rules:** Documented in `tutorial-en.ts` header (≤3 sentences, no hardcoded card facts, two-turn plan-ahead only).

## Desired change

Replace the static T6 banking insert with a contextual, first-time banking hint triggered on the first end-turn with spare actions. Add a persisted tutorial flag, wire the trigger in the turn controller (check `actionsRemaining > 0` before `processEndOfTurn`), show a HUD-highlighting overlay with cap-2 + carry-forward copy, and soften staff-first wording to "some staff grant +1, but you likely have none yet." All changes remain in tutorial copy/state/trigger only.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Add/update banking hint strings (title/body) and soften staff-first wording; follow `tutorial.<stepId>.title` / `tutorial.<stepId>.body` pattern.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialState.ts` — Add persisted flag `hasSeenBankingHint` (schema bump or additive field with legacy default), helpers to get/set it.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — Define the contextual hint's step/overlay descriptor if modeled as a step; or keep hint metadata here for the controller to consume.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` — Render the banking hint overlay and highlight the HUD/action-counter zone (`hud` / `actionButtons` zone already exists).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Gate and fire the first-bank trigger on `endTurn()` when `state.actionsRemaining > 0` and flag unset; hand off to hints/overlay without blocking turn processing.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Read-only reference for banking math; no edits expected (cap 2, bankable = min(remaining,1)).

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (done) — Main Street: action banking (parent feature; banking logic, state, persistence).
- **CG-0MT4ZHQU9003MWER** (done) — HUD banked counter + GM-aware tooltip (AC5 of parent).
- **CG-0MT4ZHR9M007VP9D** (done) — Document action banking in core rules.
- **CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W** (in_progress) — Banking-aware AI strategy (separate follow-up; not in scope here).

## Risks & assumptions

- **One-shot timing:** If the tutorial scenario always consumes the action (move Laundromat → T6), the first-bank condition may never fire in the scripted path. Copy must make sense if the player never idles; trigger simply never shows in that run — acceptable. No scenario tweak to force an idle day unless producer requests it.
- **Persistence migration:** Legacy localStorage without the new flag must default to false (hint not yet seen) and not reset completed tutorials.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Engine cap changes, HUD redesign, or AI banking behavior are out of scope — record as linked work items, don't implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (scope): "Does this include new tutorial steps, or just adding banking text to existing steps?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "Both options are viable; prefer embedding into existing steps (T6 — first End Turn) to keep tutorial length stable. A new step is only justified if the concept is too dense to share." Source: self-research of tutorial structure and editorial rules. Accepted: prefer embedding; new steps only if pedagogically necessary. **Superseded 2026-09-01:** Revised to contextual first-time trigger on `actionsRemaining > 0`; no static T6 insert.
- Q2 (scenario): "Does the current tutorial scenario produce a day where the player ends without acting (banked > 0)?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "The current scenario (T3 move Laundromat → T6 end turn) banks 0 on day 1 because the move consumes the action. Day 2 (T7 place) uses the action again. Banking is never observed. A teaching step may need a scenario adjustment — either an 'idle day' step, or a rephrased T6 body that explains banking even when banked=0." Source: self-research of TutorialScenario.ts and budget analysis in TutorialFlow.ts. Accepted: the tutorial copy should explain banking regardless of whether banked > 0 on the first pass; the scenario does not need changes unless the teaching demands an idle day (deferred if scope-creep risk). **Updated:** With contextual trigger, no idle-day scenario tweak; hint simply doesn't fire if never idle — acceptable.
- Q3 (step placement): "Where should banking be taught — T4 (Your Hand), T6 (End Turn), or a new step?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "T6 (End Turn) is the natural place: 'End the day to collect income and start the next one. Any unused actions bank up to 2 for future days.' This is concise, one-point, ≤3 sentences, and fits the editorial rules." Source: self-research of step content and action economy flow. Accepted: T6 extension preferred. **Superseded:** Now a contextual overlay triggered from `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` on first bankable end-turn, highlighting the HUD.
- Q4 (2026-09-01, producer): "Refactor from fixed step insert to contextual first-bank trigger; soften staff-first wording." — Answer (producer): Replace fixed insert with trigger firing when player ends turn with remaining action points; persistence flag prevents repeat; staff-first text clarifies some staff grant +1 but likely none at this early stage. Accepted: scope reframed to contextual hint + flag + trigger wiring + copy softening.

# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)
- Related docs (from repo scan): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` · `docs/DEVELOPER.md` · `AGENTS.md`
- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).
- Q2 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Child item coverage for AC5 — create competitive-scene child now or defer to planning?" — Answer (producer): "planning. for now what do you mean by 'owner colored streets'" → resolved as **deferred to planning**; follow-up clarification Q5 added. # Intake Brief: Enable Main Street Expansion of Playing Area

## Problem Statement

Main Street currently has a single fixed 2×5 street (10 slots) with no ability to expand the playing field. The player should be able to zoom out at any time to reveal a larger 2D grid of streets, where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots between streets are shared — one card serves all four adjacent streets, with normal adjacency rules.

## Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want to zoom out and explore neighbouring streets so that I can place more businesses and grow my empire beyond the initial 10-slot grid.
- **As a player**, I want shared corner plots between streets so that strategically placed businesses create cross-street synergy bonuses.
- **As a player**, I want the zoom to work like a map — smooth camera movement that reveals streets organically without gating or milestones.
- **As a game engine developer**, I want the grid system to be unbounded (or at least large enough to support extended play) so the game doesn't end prematurely when all streets are full.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Camera system**: A zoom/pan camera system is implemented for Main Street, allowing the player to zoom out to reveal neighbouring streets. The zoom is controlled by the player (e.g. scroll wheel or button), not gated by milestones.
2. **Grid topology**: The street grid is represented as a 2D lattice where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots (where streets meet at the corners of adjacent 2×5 grids) are shared — one card slot serves the shared position, and the card is adjacent to neighbours in all four streets per normal adjacency rules.
3. **Adjacency & synergy**: The adjacency resolver (`MainStreetAdjacency.ts`) is updated to compute correct 8-way Chebyshev adjacency across street cells, including shared corner slots. Synergy bonuses and income calculations work correctly for cards on expanded streets and shared corners.
4. **Rendering**: All street cells within the current camera viewport are rendered. Cards placed on expanded or shared slots display and interact correctly. Unrevealed streets outside the current zoom level are not rendered.
5. **Save/Load**: The expanded grid state (all placed cards, including shared corner cards, and current zoom/camera position) serializes and deserializes correctly.

## Constraints

- The zoom is **always available** — no gating by milestones, turns, or resources.
- The grid is **conceptually unbounded** (at minimum, support at least a 3×3 or 5×5 grid of streets). Practically, the grid could grow dynamically as the player zooms out further.
- Corner plots are **shared between streets**: one card slot, one card, normal adjacency rules (8-way Chebyshev) apply — the card counts as a neighbour to all adjacent slots across all streets it touches.
- The existing `GRID_SIZE = 10`, `STREET_COLS = 5`, `STREET_ROWS = 2` constants and the flat 10-slot array must be refactored to support multi-street topology.
- Must preserve deterministic seed-based gameplay and save/load compatibility.
- Existing adjacency/synergy/Income systems must continue working without modification to core logic — only the coordinate/adjacency mapping layer changes.

## Existing State

- **Single street**: `GRID_SIZE = 10`, `STREET_COLS = 5`, `STREET_ROWS = 2` (from `MainStreetConstants.ts` and `MainStreetCards.ts`).
- **Flat array**: `streetGrid` is `(BusinessCard | CommunitySpaceCard | null)[]` with row-major indexing.
- **Adjacency**: `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `toGridPosition()` maps flat index → {x, y} using `STREET_COLS = 5`; `neighbors()` computes 8-way Chebyshev distance within the 10-slot boundary.
- **Rendering**: `MainStreetRenderer.ts` and `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` position 10 slots in two rows, hardcoded layout.
- **No camera system**: Phaser camera is not used for street navigation; the game uses a fixed viewport.
- **SpatialRules**: Core engine provides `Grid<T>`, `neighbors()`, `shortestPath()` (`@core-engine/SpatialRules`) — reusable for multi-street topology.

## Desired Change

- Introduce a 2D street-cell grid where each cell is a 2×5 street (10 slots).
- Add a camera/zoom system to navigate the grid.
- Refactor the adjacency resolver to work with the 2D grid, computing correct neighbours across street cells and shared corners.
- Update rendering to draw all visible street cells within the viewport.
- Update state serialization to include the full grid and camera position.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — Refactor `STREET_COLS/ROWS` into per-street-cell dimensions; add grid dimension constants.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Update `GRID_SIZE` to a dynamic value; remove hard-coded 10-slot assumption.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Change `streetGrid` from flat array to 2D grid structure; add camera/zoom state.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Refactor `toGridPosition()`, `neighbors()` to compute positions on the 2D street-cell grid; handle shared corner slots.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Update rendering loop to iterate over visible street cells; add camera transform.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — Update layout calculations for multi-street grid.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Integrate camera control (zoom/pan input), wire up rendering and adjacency changes.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Update drop-zone and click-target logic for expanded grid.

# Review all tests — test-suite value audit with reproducible skill

## Summary

Review the entire (~476-file) test suite to evaluate whether each test actually tests something useful, classify every file against the documented low-value anti-pattern categories, produce a recommended removal/clean-up list, convert each recommendation into a child work item, and author a repo-local skill that makes the review process reproducible.

## Problem statement

The test suite has grown to ~476 `*.test.ts` files (~139k lines) — 364 unit, 112 browser, 12 E2E (incl. 6 tutorial-E2E parts), 4 smoke, plus balance/electron/scripts/replay groups — since the last full-suite cleanup (CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR removed 32 low-value files from a 344-file suite). Low-value tests (placeholder assertions, source-code-grep tests, self-referential simulations, duplicates of core coverage, type-level-only checks, zero-assertion browser tests) accumulate silently, adding maintenance cost and runtime without detecting real regressions. This item performs a fresh, reproducible audit of the whole suite and converts findings into actionable tracked work.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainers** — want a defensible, recorded basis for pruning the suite and assurance that kept tests add value.
- **AI agents / future reviewers** — need a codified, repeatable procedure so a re-audit (after more growth) is a skill invocation, not a from-scratch investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Entire-suite review completed.** Every `*.test.ts` file (all ~476, across unit/browser/E2E/smoke/balance/electron/scripts/replay) is reviewed and classified as `keep` / `remove` / `clean-up` against the anti-pattern categories reused from CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR: source-code-grep assertions, placeholder/tautological tests (`expect(true).toBe(true)`), self-referential simulations (zero production-code imports), duplicates of core coverage, type-level/structural-only tests, and zero-assertion browser tests. *Verification:* a complete classification table (file → category/decision) is present in the report, and the reviewed file count reconciles with the inventory snapshot recorded at implementation start.
- **Removal & clean-up list delivered.** A categorised list of proposed removals/clean-ups is produced as `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` and summarised in the work-item description, each entry listing file path, line count, category, and rationale. *Verification:* the report exists, is committed, and its per-category counts reconcile with the classification table.
- **Recommendations tracked as child work items.** Each removal/clean-up recommendation is created as a child work item under CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y, each with a clear goal + measurable ACs, e.g.:
  ```bash
  wl create --parent CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y --issue-type task --priority low --stage idea \
    --title "Test review: remove <group>" --description "…" --json
  ```
  **No test file is deleted or modified by this item itself** — the children carry out the changes. *Verification:* `wl show CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y --children --json` lists the recommendation items and the repo diff for this item contains no test deletions/edits (only report, skill, docs).
- **Reproducible skill authored.** A repo-local skill `/skill:test-review` is created at `.pi/skills/test-review/SKILL.md` (project skill conventions: front-matter `name` + `description`, markdown body, optional `scripts/`) codifying the methodology — anti-pattern categories, the exact discovery commands (grep/find patterns), classification steps, report format, and the child-work-item creation convention. *Verification:* the skill's documented procedure is exercised end-to-end during implementation to reproduce (a subset of) the audit on a clean checkout, and the skill is registered in docs.
- **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes — the review process, report, and the new `test-review` skill referenced in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and/or `AGENTS.md`. *Verification:* docs committed in the same change; no stale references to reviewed/removed files remain.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** (Release quality gate; `npm test -- --project unit` minimum before push — see AGENTS.md.) *Verification:* `npm test -- --project unit` is green at completion.

## Constraints

- Investigation scope is the **entire** suite (producer-confirmed); no area of the repo is exempt.
- This item is analysis + recommendation + skill authoring only — it must not itself remove or modify tests (producer-confirmed deliverable shape: create work items for recommendations).
- Reuse the anti-pattern categories and reporting style of CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR for continuity (producer-confirmed); this is a fresh pass over the grown suite, not a duplicate.
- Tests guarding historical regressions, documented precedents (e.g. the 2026-07-31 cleanup's reference list), and tests with explicit work-item linkage should be treated as `keep` unless evidence shows they no longer assert anything.
- UK English in all written output; work-item descriptions/comments in Markdown; ignore-rule compliance when scanning the repo.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Subjective classification risk (scope: whole review).** "Useful" is a judgement call. *Mitigation:* every classification carries an evidence line (file, lines, category, observed pattern); when evidence is ambiguous the file defaults to `keep` and is noted as `uncertain` rather than proposed for removal. Median, conservative posture — prefer a false negative to a false removal.
- **Risk of deleting a regression guard.** *Mitigation:* flagged removals are recommendations only and are executed by child work items through the normal implement → audit gate; a reviewer sees the full list before any deletion lands.
- **Browser/E2E static-review limits.** The 112 browser + 12 E2E files cannot be valued purely by static inspection. *Assumption:* classification there uses structure/assertion inspection and run-cost evidence; anything uncertain is `keep` with a `needs-manual-verification` note.
- **Scope-creep risk.** The review will surface adjacent opportunities (test-helper deduplication, fixture consolidation, runtime tuning). *Mitigation:* record these as separate linked work items (`discovered-from:CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y`), never as additional scope inside this item.
- **Inventory drift.** The suite grew from 344 → 476 files between cleanups and will keep growing. *Assumption:* the reviewed snapshot is the commit at implementation start, and the report records that commit hash; the new skill is the mechanism for refreshing the audit later.
- **Skill-staleness risk.** A written procedure can drift from the suite it describes. *Mitigation:* the skill documents the discovery commands and the report format, and the report records inventory counts, so a re-run diffs cleanly.
- **Overlap risk with CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR.** *Mitigation:* the report treats the 2026-07-31 removals as already-handled and re-audits only what exists today; near-misses are compared against that item's taxonomy for consistency.

## Existing state

- 476 `*.test.ts` files (~139k lines) under `tests/` across unit/browser/E2E/smoke/balance/electron/scripts/replay groups (counts verified at intake, 2026-09-15).
- Prior full-suite cleanup: CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR (completed, 2026-07-31) removed 32 files (~3,806 lines) and stripped dead assertions from 8 kept files; its category list is the reference taxonomy for this audit.

Prime removal/clean-up candidate to verify first.
- Repo-local skills precedent: `.pi/skills/release-windows/`, `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/` (front-matter + markdown body + optional `scripts/`); documented in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Desired change

- A committed, versioned audit report (`docs/dev/test-suite-review.md`) that a future agent can re-run and diff against.
- A `test-review` skill that automates/codifies the re-audit so the entire process is reproducible on demand.
- Child work items (one per recommendation or recommendation group) that carry out the removals/clean-ups through the normal implement workflow.

```bash

git rev-parse HEAD
find tests -name '*.test.ts' -type f | wc -l

# Discovery probes used for classification
grep -rc 'expect(true)\.toBe(true)' tests --include='*.test.ts' | grep -v ':0'
grep -rl 'readFileSync' tests --include='*.test.ts'
```

# Tax Audit should collect 45% of banked coins

## Problem statement

The Main Street Tax Audit incident currently charges a flat 300-coin penalty
(`card-data.csv` row `evt-tax`, `coinDelta = -300`). A flat fee is regressive:
it is trivial for a late-game player with thousands of banked coins and
crippling for an early-game player with a few hundred. The Tax Audit should
instead scale with the player's wealth — collecting **45% of banked coins** —
so the consequence stays meaningful at every stage. Employing the **Accountant**
staff card should soften the blow, reducing the rate to **25%**.

## Users

- **Players** — Want incidents that scale with their economic position so a
  tax audit remains a real setback late-game and is survivable early-game.
- **Players who hire the Accountant** — Want that hiring decision to have a
  tangible, thematic payoff (tax mitigation) in addition to its existing
  market-refresh discount.
- **AI / Monte Carlo balance harness** — Needs the projected cost of the Tax
  Audit (and its Accept/Reject chain evaluation) to reflect the percentage
  mechanic, so simulations stay accurate.
- **TCE developers / producers** — Need a data-driven, testable mechanic that
  extends the existing `EventCard` model without breaking flat-delta events.

### User stories

- "As a player, I want a Tax Audit to take a proportional share of my banked
  coins, so the penalty is fair whether I am rich or poor."
- "As a player, I want hiring the Accountant to reduce my Tax Audit rate from
  45% to 25%, so the staff card feels worth its cost."
- "As an AI player, I want the projected cost of a Tax Audit to use the same
  percentage math as the live game, so my accept/reject decisions are correct."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Percentage collection** — When the Tax Audit (`evt-tax`) incident resolves
   on the Accept path, the coin loss equals **45% of the player's banked coins
   at resolution time** (`state.resourceBank.coins` before the effect).
   *Verification:* unit test seeds a known coin balance, forces `evt-tax`,
   accepts, and asserts the exact resulting balance.
2. **Accountant mitigation** — When the player has the Accountant staff card,
   the Tax Audit rate is **25%** instead of 45%. *Verification:* unit test with
   the Accountant employed asserts a 25% balance delta.
3. **No negative balance** — The coin loss is clamped so `resourceBank.coins`
   never drops below 0 (a tax audit cannot bankrupt a player into negative
   coins). *Verification:* unit test with a low balance asserts the floor at 0.
4. **Pre-existing flat-delta events unchanged** — All other events (including
   the rest of the Tax Escalation chain: `evt-tax-error`, `evt-tax-inquiry`)
   continue to apply their flat `coinDelta` values exactly as before.
   *Verification:* regression test asserting an unchanged flat event's delta.
5. **AI projection parity** — `projectEventCoinDelta()` (used for AI
   affordability/accept-reject decisions) returns the same percentage-based
   magnitude for the Tax Audit as the live resolution path.
   *Verification:* unit test asserting projection equals the applied delta.
6. **Tests** — Unit tests cover percentage resolution, Accountant mitigation,
   zero-balance clamping, flat-event regression, and AI-projection parity.
   *Verification:* targeted `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/`.
7. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
8. **Full suite** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Data-driven** — The 45% / 25% rates must be defined as named constants
  (not magic literals scattered through the engine) and referenced from the
  card data or a single config site.
- **Backward compatible** — Existing saves and cards without the new
  percentage field must load and behave exactly as before. The new fields must
  be optional.
- **Deterministic** — The percentage calculation must not consume RNG (it is
  derived from the coin balance), preserving replay/transcript determinism.
- **Chain semantics preserved** — The Accept/Reject dual-choice behaviour of
  the Tax Escalation chain (CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128) is unchanged; only the
  magnitude of the Accept effect changes.
- **Formatting** — The activity-log line for the Tax Audit must show the
  actual coins lost (e.g. "Tax Audit (-225 coins)"), consistent with existing
  `describeEventEffects` output.

## Existing state

- **Tax Audit card**: `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` line 42 —
  `event,evt-tax,Tax Audit,...,All,,-300,0,...,true,,evt-tax-inquiry,,` — flat
  `coinDelta = -300`, `hasChoices = true`, `acceptNextCardId = null`,
  `rejectNextCardId = evt-tax-inquiry`.
- **EventCard model**: `MainStreetCards.ts:385` — `coinDelta: number` and
  `reputationDelta: number` only; no percentage field. `hasChoices`,
  `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId` added by CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128.
- **Event resolution**: `MainStreetEngine.ts` `resolveEvent()` (~line 546)
  applies `state.resourceBank.coins += applyReputationMultiplier(cDelta(event.coinDelta), ...)`
  for `target: 'All'`; staff incident mitigation (`computeIncidentSkillBuffs`)
  already reduces negative incident coin deltas by a percentage.
- **Choice resolution**: `MainStreetEngine.ts` `resolveEventChoice()` (~line 2088)
  calls `resolveEvent()` on Accept and skips it on Reject.
- **AI projection**: `MainStreetEngine.ts:2212` `projectEventCoinDelta()` and
  `eventSeverity()` (~2237) read `event.coinDelta` directly.
- **Accountant card**: `card-data.csv` line 141 — `staff-accountant` with
  `refreshCostDiscount` only (`StaffCard.refreshCostDiscount`,
  `MainStreetCards.ts:557`). "Adds +1 hand slot and makes investment refreshes
  cost 1 less."
- **Difficulty config**: `MainStreetDifficulty.ts` has incident draw pacing
  parameters but no per-event percentage rates.

## Desired change

1. **Card data** — Add an optional percentage field to the event card model
   (e.g. `coinPercentDelta?: number`, value `-0.45` for Tax Audit) and set it
   on `evt-tax` in `card-data.csv` (new column). Update the CSV header and the
   `EventCard` interface/serialisation in `MainStreetCards.ts`.
2. **Engine resolution** — In `resolveEvent()`, when an event carries a
   percentage delta, compute the coin loss from the pre-effect
   `resourceBank.coins`, clamp at 0, and log the actual amount. Flat-delta
   events take the existing path.
3. **Accountant mitigation** — Add a staff-level tax-rate override (e.g.
   `taxAuditRate?: number` / `taxPctDiscount?: number` on `StaffCard`, aggregated
   across `state.staffCards`) so an employed Accountant sets the Tax Audit rate
   to 25%. The engine applies it when resolving the percentage event.
4. **AI projection** — Update `projectEventCoinDelta()` / `eventSeverity()` to
   mirror the percentage math for percentage events.
5. **Tests** — New unit tests for the five verification points in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Add percentage field/column; set
  Tax Audit to 45%; add Accountant tax-rate field if card-level.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Extend `EventCard` with
  `coinPercentDelta?`; extend `StaffCard` with the tax-rate field; parse from CSV.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `resolveEvent()` percentage
  branch + clamping; `projectEventCoinDelta()` / `eventSeverity()` parity;
  Accountant-rate lookup.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — (only if a typed config field
  is needed for defaults; otherwise untouched).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — Likely home for a
  `computeTaxAuditRate(staffCards)` helper, consistent with existing staff-buff
  helpers.
- `tests/main-street/` — New/updated unit tests (percentage resolution,
  Accountant mitigation, clamping, flat-event regression, AI parity).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — rounding mode is `Math.round`** (standard). The engine already
  uses an integer-rounding helper for fractional effects; the same convention
  is assumed. **OPEN QUESTION Q1** — producer to confirm.
- **Assumption — no minimum beyond the 0 floor**: the tax can round to 0 for a
  player with very few coins; there is no "always at least 1" rule.
  **OPEN QUESTION Q2** — producer to confirm.
- **Assumption — scope is Tax Audit only**: the percentage mechanic applies to
  `evt-tax` only; `evt-tax-error` (-200) and `evt-tax-inquiry` (-600) keep
  their flat values (AC4). **OPEN QUESTION Q3** — producer to confirm whether
  the whole Tax Escalation chain should convert.
- **Assumption — Accountant mechanism is a card-level numeric field** (Option A,
  mirroring `refreshCostDiscount`) rather than a new specialization skill.
  **OPEN QUESTION Q4** — producer to confirm.
- **Assumption — rates are difficulty-independent**: 45% / 25% are fixed for
  Easy/Medium/Hard. **OPEN QUESTION Q5** — producer to confirm.
- **Risk — ordering vs `applyReputationMultiplier`**: the percentage must be
  computed from the pre-effect balance, then the reputation multiplier applied
  in the same order as existing deltas. Mitigation: a focused test with
  non-default reputation.
- **Risk — AI/Renderer divergence**: the Tax Audit magnitude appears in the
  engine, the AI projection, and possibly the renderer/animator. Mitigation:
  route all three through one shared helper.
- **Risk — scope creep**: converting the full Tax Escalation chain (and other
  events) is a natural follow-on; recorded as a separate work item if the
  producer wants it, not folded into this change.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128** — Story-driven event chains with dual-choice
  consequences (completed) — defines the Tax Escalation chain and the
  Accept/Reject path that this item's effect feeds into.
- **CG-0MM8RAXJ61L6BG8Z** — Rework event system: reclassify triggers, incident
  queue, investments row, player hand UI (completed) — Tax Audit classified as
  an Incident.
- **CG-0MM8RCFZU03GY009** — Reclassify event triggers and rename Rainy Night
  (completed).
- **CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58** — Content: New chain cards and retro-fitting (open) —
  the Tax Escalation chain source.
- **CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4** — Accountant refresh-discount ability (Group F) —
  the existing Accountant staff buff this change builds alongside.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1 — Rounding:** When 45% (or 25%) of banked coins produces a fractional
  result, which rounding mode should be used?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used to draft: `Math.round()` (standard), matching the engine's
    existing integer-rounding convention. Recorded on the work item for
    producer confirmation.
- **Q2 — Minimum/Maximum bounds:** Should the tax be floored at 0, floored at
  1 coin, or capped at the total balance?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: clamp the loss so coins never go below 0 (no negative
    balance); no "at least 1" floor.
- **Q3 — Chain cards:** Apply the percentage to Tax Audit only, or to all three
  Tax Escalation cards (`evt-tax-error`, `evt-tax`, `evt-tax-inquiry`)?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: Tax Audit only (per the work-item title); the other two
    keep flat values.
- **Q4 — Accountant mechanism:** How should the 45%→25% reduction be
  represented — a card-level numeric field, a specialization skill, or
  another mechanism?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: card-level numeric field on `StaffCard` (Option A),
    mirroring the existing `refreshCostDiscount` pattern.
- **Q5 — Difficulty scaling:** Are 45% / 25% fixed across Easy/Medium/Hard, or
  difficulty-scaled?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: fixed across all difficulties.
- **Q6 — Research:** Inspected `card-data.csv` (Tax Audit `evt-tax` row; Tax
  Escalation rows `evt-tax-error`/`evt-tax-inquiry`; `staff-accountant` row),
  `MainStreetCards.ts` (`EventCard`, `StaffCard`, `refreshCostDiscount`),
  `MainStreetEngine.ts` (`resolveEvent`, `resolveEventChoice`,
  `projectEventCoinDelta`, `eventSeverity`), `MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`,
  `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`, and related work item CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128.
  Confirmed: banked coins = `state.resourceBank.coins`; Tax Audit is a
  `target: 'All'` Incident with an Accept/Reject chain; no existing
  percentage-of-balance event effect exists.

# Intake Brief — REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own projects. (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17)

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine is a single flat monorepo where every example game is co-located with the shared engine code. This couples game development to the full repository, makes it hard to version or reuse the engine independently, and prevents building lean distributions that bundle only a selected subset of games.

## Users

- **Engine maintainer (primary)** — Maintains shared engine modules and the Gym demo suite; wants a standalone core-engine repo that can evolve, be versioned, and be pulled into any distribution without dragging all games along.
  - *Story:* As an engine maintainer I can work on `src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai` and the Gym in one repo, so that engine changes do not require touching game repos.
- **Game developer** — Builds a single example game in isolation; wants to check out just that game plus the engine and run `npm run dev` / `npm test` / `npm run build` without cloning every other game.
  - *Story:* As a game developer I can clone `tce-golf` (or any game repo) which pulls the core engine as a submodule, so that I can iterate on that game with a fast, focused checkout (`tce-game = distribution with 1 game`).
- **Distribution builder / launcher maintainer** — Assembles and ships a playable bundle (web + desktop binary) that contains the core engine plus a chosen set of 1..n games.
  - *Story:* As a distribution builder I can configure which game submodules are checked out in the launcher repo and run `npm run build` / `npm run package` to produce a web build and an Electron binary that show only the included games in the Game Selector.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Core-engine repo defined and extractable** — A standalone core-engine repository exists (or a concrete extraction plan + script is delivered) containing everything shared across games: `src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai`, `src/balance-cards` (if shared), the Gym (`example-games/gym`), the launcher shell (`src/ui/GameSelectorScene`, `src/ui/createCardGame`), Electron launcher (`electron/`), shared assets under `public/assets`, and shared configs (`tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `package.json` engine dependencies). Git history for moved files is preserved where feasible.
2. **Per-game repos with reverse submodule** — Each example game (golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto) has its own GitHub repo with a consistent layout that pulls the core engine as a git submodule for standalone development; `npm install`, `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, and `npm test -- --project unit` (or equivalent targeted run) succeed in a `game + engine` checkout and path aliases (`@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`, `@ai/*`) resolve correctly across the submodule boundary. Documented exception: games may vendor only their own `example-games/<game>/` tree.
3. **Launcher distribution assembles N games via submodules** — The main Tableau-Card-Engine repo acts as the launcher/distribution repo: it bundles the core engine plus a configurable set of games checked out as git submodules (e.g. under `games/` or `example-games/`), the Game Selector enumerates only the checked-out games, and `npm run build` (web, `dist/` with `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` base) and `npm run build:electron` / `npm run package` (desktop binary via Electron) succeed for any selection of 1..n games including the boundary cases of 1 game and all games.
4. **Dev workflows and Gym preserved** — `npm run dev` (HMR on port 3000), `vite`/`tsconfig` alias resolution, and the Gym demo scenes all continue to work from the core-engine repo and from the launcher distribution; Gym remains the canonical core-engine feature demonstrator and does not move to a game repo.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — `npm run build` succeeds and the relevant test profile passes in the launcher distribution with its default game set (full suite on release; unit + build at minimum before any push per AGENTS.md quality gates).

## Constraints

- Integration mechanism is **git submodules** (option a) — not npm packages or npm workspaces. No npm publication of the engine in this phase.
- **No CI required** in this phase — neither the core-engine repo nor the per-game repos need new GitHub Actions pipelines; existing `pr-checks.yml` / `package.yml` / `deploy.yml` remain on the launcher repo as-is.
- The launcher repo remains the deployable web + Electron distribution; game repos do not deploy independently.
- Preserve permissive-license posture (MIT / CC0) and existing toolchain (Phaser 4 RC, TypeScript strict, Vite, Vitest, Electron).
- Avoid breaking existing developer workflows more than necessary; submodule setup must be documented with copy-paste commands (`git clone --recurse-submodules`, `git submodule update --init --recursive`).
- Keep changes surgical — do not speculatively introduce versioning, changelogs, or release automation beyond what is needed to make the submodule composition build.

## Existing State

- Flat monorepo with a single `package.json` (v0.1.15), single `vite.config.ts` (path aliases for `@core-engine`, `@card-system`, `@rule-engine`, `@ui`, `@ai`), single `tsconfig.json`, and single `index.html` / `main.ts` unified entry point that hard-imports every game scene and registers them in `GAMES` for `GameSelectorScene`.
- Shared engine code under `src/` (`core-engine`, `card-system`, `rule-engine`, `ui`, `ai`, `balance-cards`); example games under `example-games/` (gym, golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto); Gym is the interactive demo suite for core-engine features.
- Electron launcher under `electron/` with `build:electron` / `start:electron` / `package` scripts; `.gitmodules` does not exist; production build targets GitHub Pages at `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` and desktop binaries via `electron-builder`.
- Tests under `tests/` with Vitest projects (unit, browser, smoke, dev, tutorial E2E); game scenes and core modules are tightly coupled via static imports in `main.ts`.

## Desired Change

- Extract a **core-engine repository** that owns all shared code plus Gym and the launcher shell (GameSelector, Electron host). The extraction should be reproducible and preserve history (e.g. via `git filter-repo` / `git subtree` or a documented manual move — exact tooling is an implementation detail but must be recorded).
- Move each **example game to its own GitHub repo** (one repo per game, consistent layout). Each game repo composes a runnable project by pulling the core engine as a git submodule — i.e. a game checkout is itself a minimal TCE distribution with 1 game. Submodule pointer + local Vite/TS configs make engine imports resolve without publishing a package.
- Retain the **main Tableau-Card-Engine repo as the launcher/distribution repo** that composes the core engine with any subset of game submodules. Provide a simple mechanism (submodule presence, config file, or CLI flag) to specify which games are included in a given build, so `npm run build` and `npm run package` produce a distribution containing exactly 1..n games (web + binary). The Game Selector must discover games dynamically from the checked-out set rather than hardcoding all imports.
